'''Endre Szemerédi''' ({{IPA|hu|ˈɛndrɛ ˈsɛmɛreːdi|lang}}; born August 21, 1940) is a Hungarian-American<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nepszava.hu/articles/article.php?id=532617|title=Magyar tudós kapta a matematika Nobel-díját|publisher=[[Népszava]]|date=March 21, 2012|access-date=April 19, 2012|language=hu|archive-date=June 10, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120610091436/http://www.nepszava.hu/articles/article.php?id=532617|url-status=dead}}</ref> mathematician and [[computer scientist]], working in the field of [[combinatorics]] and [[theoretical computer science]]. He is the State of New Jersey Professor of Computer Science Emeritus at [[Rutgers University]], after having served in the position since 1986. He also holds a professor emeritus status at the [[Alfréd Rényi Institute of Mathematics]] of the [[Hungarian Academy of Sciences]].

Szemerédi has won prizes in mathematics and science, including the [[Abel Prize]] in 2012. He has made a number of discoveries in combinatorics and computer science, including [[Szemerédi's theorem]], the [[Szemerédi regularity lemma]], the [[Erdős–Szemerédi theorem]], the [[Hajnal–Szemerédi theorem]] and the [[Szemerédi–Trotter theorem]].

==Early life==
Szemerédi was born in [[Budapest]]. Since his parents wished him to become a doctor, Szemerédi enrolled at a college of medicine, but he dropped out after six months (in an interview<ref>By Gabor Stockert</ref> he explained it: "I was not sure I could do work bearing such responsibility.").<ref name="ams">{{citation|first1=Martin|last1=Raussen|first2=Christian|last2=Skau|url=https://www.ams.org/notices/201302/rnoti-p221.pdf|journal=[[Notices of the American Mathematical Society]]|title=Interview with Endre Szemerédi|volume=60|year=2013|issue=2|pages=221–231|doi=10.1090/noti948|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.heidelberg-laureate-forum.org/blog/laureate/endre-szemeredi/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130925100341/http://www.heidelberg-laureate-forum.org/blog/laureate/endre-szemeredi/ |archive-date=September 25, 2013 |title=Endre Szemerédi › Heidelberg Laureate Forum}}</ref><ref>[http://nopr.niscair.res.in/bitstream/123456789/16108/1/SR%2050%282%29%2016-18.pdf Sunita Chand; Ramesh Chandra Parida . ''Science Reporter'', February 2013, p. 17]</ref> He studied at the [[ELTE Faculty of Sciences|Faculty of Sciences]] of the  [[Eötvös Loránd University]] in Budapest and received his PhD from [[Moscow State University]]. His adviser was [[Israel Gelfand]].<ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=70200}}</ref> This stemmed from a misspelling, as Szemerédi originally wanted to study with [[Alexander Gelfond]].<ref name="ams"/>

==Academic career==
Szemerédi has been the State of New Jersey Professor of computer science at [[Rutgers University]] since 1986. He has held visiting positions at [[Stanford University]] (1974), [[McGill University]] (1980), the [[University of South Carolina]] (1981–1983) and the [[University of Chicago]] (1985–1986).<ref>{{cite book
 | last1 = Holden | first1 = Helge
 | last2 = Piene | first2 = Ragni
 | contribution = Curriculum Vitae for Endre Szemerédi
 | date = August 2013
 | doi = 10.1007/978-3-642-39449-2_27
 | isbn = 9783642394492
 | pages = 507–508
 | publisher = Springer Berlin Heidelberg
 | title = The Abel Prize 2008-2012}}</ref>

==Work==
Endre Szemerédi has published over 200 scientific articles in the fields of discrete mathematics, theoretical computer science, arithmetic combinatorics and discrete geometry. He is best known for his proof from 1975 of an old conjecture of [[Paul Erdős]] and [[Pál Turán]]: if a sequence of natural numbers has positive [[upper density]] then it contains arbitrarily long [[arithmetic progression]]s. This is now known as [[Szemerédi's theorem]]. One of the lemmas introduced in his proof is now known as the [[Szemerédi regularity lemma]], which has become an important lemma in [[combinatorics]], being used for instance in [[property testing]] for graphs and in the theory of [[graph limit]]s.

He is also known for the [[Szemerédi–Trotter theorem]] in [[Incidence geometry (structure)|incidence geometry]] and the [[Hajnal–Szemerédi theorem]] and [[Ruzsa–Szemerédi problem]] in [[graph theory]]. [[Miklós Ajtai]] and Szemerédi proved the [[corners theorem]], an important step toward higher-dimensional generalizations of the [[Szemerédi's theorem|Szemerédi theorem]]. With Ajtai and [[János Komlós (mathematician)|János Komlós]] he proved the ''ct''<sup>2</sup>/log ''t'' upper bound for the [[Ramsey number]] ''R''(3,''t''), and constructed a [[sorting network]] of optimal depth. With Ajtai, [[Václav Chvátal]], and [[Monty Newborn|Monroe M. Newborn]], Szemerédi proved the famous [[crossing number inequality]], that a [[Graph (discrete mathematics)|graph]] with ''n'' vertices and ''m'' edges, where {{nowrap|''m'' > 4''n''}} has at least {{nowrap|''m''<sup>3</sup> / 64''n''<sup>2</sup>}} [[Crossing lemma|crossings]].  With [[Paul Erdős]], he proved the [[Erdős–Szemerédi theorem]] on the number of sums and products in a finite set. With Wolfgang Paul, [[Nick Pippenger]], and [[William T. Trotter|William Trotter]], he established a separation between [[Non-deterministic Turing machine|nondeterministic]] [[linear time]] and [[Deterministic computation|deterministic]] linear time,<ref>{{Cite conference|url=https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/4568107|title=On determinism versus non-determinism and related problems|author1=Wolfgang J. Paul|author2 = [[Nick Pippenger]]|author3 = Endre Szemerédi|author4= [[William T. Trotter]]|year=1983|conference=[[Symposium on Foundations of Computer Science|Annual Symposium on Foundations of Computer Science]]}}</ref> in the spirit of the infamous [[P versus NP problem]].

==Awards and honors==
Szemerédi has won numerous awards and honors for his contribution to mathematics and computer science. A few of them are listed here:
* Honorary [[John von Neumann Professor]] (2021) <ref name="John von Neumann Professor">Recipients are listed on Budapest University of Technology and Economics website: {{cite web |url=https://www.bme.hu/John-von-Neumann-Professors |title=John von Neumann Professors |publisher=[[Budapest University of Technology and Economics]] |access-date=September 12, 2022 |archive-date=September 12, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220912204535/https://www.bme.hu/John-von-Neumann-Professors |url-status=dead }}</ref>
* Grünwald Prize (1967)<ref name="2012 Abel Prize Szemerédi">{{cite web | title=2012: Endre Szemerédi Biography
 | url=https://abelprize.no/sites/default/files/2021-04/Abel%20prize%202012%20Endre%20Szemeredi%20Biography%20eng.pdf | access-date=2023-12-26}}</ref>
* Grünwald Prize (1968)<ref name="2012 Abel Prize Szemerédi"/>
* [[Alfréd Rényi Prize|Rényi Prize]] (1973)<ref name="Rényi Prize 1973">{{cite web | title=Endre Szemerédi | website=Rényi | url=https://www.renyi.hu/en/researchers/endre-szemeredi | access-date=2023-12-26}}</ref>
* [[George Pólya Prize]] for Achievement in Applied Combinatorics (SIAM),<ref name="SIAM 2017">{{cite web | title=George Pólya Prize in Applied Combinatorics | website=SIAM | date=May 26, 2017 | url=https://www.siam.org/prizes-recognition/major-prizes-lectures/detail/george-polya-prize-applied-combinatorics | access-date=August 21, 2022}}</ref> (1975)
* Prize of the Hungarian Academy of Sciences (1979)<ref name="2012 Abel Prize Szemerédi"/>
* State of New Jersey Professorship (1986)<ref name="Szemeredi Rutgers">{{cite web | last=Szemeredi | first=Endre | title=Szemeredi, Endre | website=Home | date=August 21, 2022 | url=https://www.cs.rutgers.edu/people/professors/details/emeritus/endre-szemeredi | access-date=August 21, 2022}}</ref>
* The [[Leroy P. Steele Prize]] for Seminal Contribution to Research (AMS),<ref name="American Mathematical Society 2018">{{cite web | title=Browse Prizes and Awards | website=American Mathematical Society | date=November 26, 2018 | url=https://www.ams.org/prizes-awards/pabrowse.cgi?parent_id=27 | access-date=August 21, 2022}}</ref> (2008)
* The Rolf Schock Prize in Mathematics for deep and pioneering work from 1975 on arithmetic progressions in subsets of the integers (2008)<ref>{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20120906122830/http://www.mta.hu/index.php?id=858&tt_news=7654|title=Major US Maths Prize Given to HAS Full Member}}, Hungarian Academy of Sciences, January 9, 2008.</ref>
* The [[Széchenyi Prize]] of the Hungarian Republic for his many fundamental contributions to mathematics and computer science (2012)<ref name=ae/>
* The [[Abel Prize]] for his fundamental contributions to discrete mathematics and theoretical computer science (2012)<ref name="The Abel Prize 2012">{{cite web | title=2012: Endre Szemerédi | website=The Abel Prize | date=August 21, 2022 | url=https://abelprize.no/abel-prize-laureates/2012 | access-date=August 21, 2022}}</ref>
* [[Hungarian Order of Saint Stephen]]<ref name="ÓU 2020">{{cite web | title=Óbudai Egyetem: Tehetség. Siker. Közösség | website=ÓU | date=September 16, 2020 | url=https://uni-obuda.hu/2020/09/16/doctor-honoris-causa-of-obuda-university-endre-szemeredi-received-this-years-medal-of-st-stephens-order/ | access-date=August 21, 2022}}</ref>(2020)

Szemerédi is a corresponding member (1982), and member (1987) of the [[Hungarian Academy of Sciences]] and a member (2010) of the [[United States National Academy of Sciences]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/endre-szemeredi-ahw2yy/|title=Endre Szemerédi|work=Member directory|publisher=National Academy of Sciences|access-date=2024-03-31}}</ref> He was elected to the [[Academia Europaea]] in 2022.<ref name=ae>{{citation|url=https://www.ae-info.org/ae/Member/Szemer%C3%A9di_Endre|title=Endre Szemerédi|work=Members|publisher=Academia Europaea|access-date=2024-03-31}}</ref> He is also a member of the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] in [[Princeton, New Jersey]] and a permanent research fellow at the [[Alfréd Rényi Institute of Mathematics]] in Budapest.  He was the Fairchild Distinguished Scholar at the [[California Institute of Technology]] in 1987–88.
He is an honorary doctor<ref>{{cite web| url=http://kam.mff.cuni.cz/conferences/endrehc/|title=Doctor honoris causa Endre Szemerédi|date=June 15–16, 2010}}</ref> of [[Charles University]] in Prague.
He was the lecturer in the Forty-Seventh Annual DeLong Lecture Series<ref name=delong>[http://math.colorado.edu/~rmg/delong/ DeLong Lecture Series]. Math.colorado.edu. Retrieved on March 22, 2012.</ref> at the [[University of Colorado]].  He is also a recipient of the Aisenstadt Chair at CRM,<ref>[http://www.crm.umontreal.ca/Chaires/chairesPrec_an.shtml Aisenstadt Chair Recipients]. Crm.umontreal.ca. Retrieved on March 22, 2012.</ref> [[University of Montreal]]. In 2008 he was the Eisenbud Professor at the [[Mathematical Sciences Research Institute]] in [[Berkeley, California]].

In 2012, Szemerédi was awarded the [[Abel Prize]] "for his fundamental contributions to discrete mathematics and theoretical computer science, and in recognition of the profound and lasting impact of these contributions on [[additive number theory]] and [[ergodic theory]]"<ref name=abel>{{cite web|title=Hungarian-American Endre Szemerédi named Abel Prize winner|url=http://www.abelprize.no/nyheter/vis.html?tid=54138|publisher=The Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters|access-date=March 21, 2012|archive-date=August 30, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120830095113/http://www.abelprize.no/nyheter/vis.html?tid=54138|url-status=dead}}</ref> The Abel Prize citation also credited Szemerédi with bringing combinatorics to the centre-stage of mathematics and noted his place in the tradition of Hungarian mathematicians such as [[George Pólya]] who emphasized a problem-solving approach to mathematics.<ref name=hindu>{{cite news|last=Ramachandran|first=R.|title=Hungarian mathematician Endre Szemerédi gets 2012 Abel Prize|url=http://www.thehindu.com/news/article3025783.ece?homepage=true|access-date=March 22, 2012|newspaper=The Hindu|date=March 22, 2012}}</ref> Szemerédi reacted to the announcement by saying that "It is not my own personal achievement, but recognition for this field of mathematics and Hungarian mathematicians," that gave him the most pleasure.<ref name=nj.com>{{cite news|last=Ellis-Nutt|first=Amy|title=Rutgers math professor's discovery earns prestigious award, $1M prize|url=http://www.nj.com/news/index.ssf/2012/03/rutgers_math_professors_discov.html|access-date=March 22, 2012|newspaper=NJ.com|date=March 22, 2012}}</ref>

==Conferences==
[[File:AnIrregularMindBookCoverFairUse.jpg|thumb|An Irregular Mind (2010 book cover)]]

On August 2–7, 2010, the [[Alfréd Rényi Institute of Mathematics]] and the [[János Bolyai Mathematical Society]] organized a conference in honor of the 70th birthday of Endre Szemerédi.<ref>[http://www.renyi.hu/conferences/sze70/ Szemerédi is 70]. Renyi.hu. Retrieved on March 22, 2012.</ref>

Prior to the conference a volume of the Bolyai Society Mathematical Studies Series, ''An Irregular Mind'', a collection of papers edited by [[Imre Bárány]] and [[József Solymosi]], was published to celebrate Szemerédi's achievements on the occasion of his 70th birthday.<ref>{{cite book
 | last1 = Bárány | first1 = Imre
 | last2 = Solymosi | first2 = József
 | last3 = Sági | first3 = Gábor
 | doi = 10.1007/978-3-642-14444-8
 | publisher = Springer Berlin Heidelberg
 | title = An Irregular Mind: Szemerédi is 70
 | series = Bolyai Society Mathematical Studies
 | year = 2010| volume = 21
 | isbn = 978-3-642-14443-1
 }}</ref>  Another conference devoted to celebrating Szemerédi's work is
the Third Abel Conference: A Mathematical Celebration of Endre Szemerédi.<ref>[http://www.ima.umn.edu/2012-2013/SW11.29-12.1.12/ Third Abel Conference: A Mathematical Celebration of Endre Szemerédi]</ref>

==Personal life==
Szemerédi is married to Anna Kepes; they have five children, Andrea, Anita, Peter, Kati, and Zsuzsi.<ref name=delong /><ref name="The Abel Prize 2008-2012">{{cite book | title=The Abel Prize 2008–2012 | chapter=2012 Endre Szemeredi | publisher=Springer Berlin Heidelberg | publication-place=Berlin, Heidelberg | date=August 9, 2013 | isbn=978-3-642-39448-5 | issn=2661-829X | doi=10.1007/978-3-642-39449-2 | page=451}}</ref>
